questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. No version of the origin of California’s name has been fully accepted, but there is wide support for the contention that it derived from an early 16th-century Spanish novel.

B. California is a constituent state of the United States of America.

C. It was admitted as the 31st state of the union on 9 September 1850 and by the early 1960s it was the most populous U.S. state.

D. The influence of the Spanish settlers of the 18th and 19th centuries is evident in California’s architecture and place-names.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In order to solve the jumbled sentences, we should always find out the first sentence that would be the introductory sentence.
 
 
• Here the sentence **"B" **is the introductory sentence as it talks about "California".
 
 
 
• Most of the time, second sentence can be found with the help of link and usage of pronoun in the sentence.
 
 
• The sentence **"C" **starts with the pronoun **"it"** and explains more about "California"
 
 
 
• The third sentence will always explain more about the part of the second sentence.
 
 
• The sentence **"A" **explains more about "California and how this name was derived".
 
 
 
• Finally, we are left with the last sentence *i.e. ***"D".**

Hence, the right order to form a meaningful paragraph is **"BCAD".**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Kunal did not anticipate the need, __so he did not carries his own__ water bottle.

options.text: so he does not carry his own
so he did not carry his own
so he did not carried his own

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"****Option 2"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• It can be understood that the given sentence is in **"past indefinite tense"** due to the usage of **"did not"**.
 
• There will be **"did not & verb 1st form" **in the negative sentence of **past indefinite tense.**
 
• For example, I **did not go** to school yesterday due to a high fever.
 
• Let's look at the options:
 
 
• Option 1 "**so he does not carry his own**" is in the **present tense** that **does not match with the main sentence** so it's incorrect.
 
• Option 3 "**so he did not carried his own**" is incorrect because "There should be **did not and verb 1st form in past indefinite tense**".
 
• Option 2 "**so he did not carry his own**" is correct because it's in **the past tense** that makes the main sentence meaningful.
 
 

Hence, the correct sentence is "*Kunal did not anticipate the need, so he did not carry his own water bottle".*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

They said that they would issue the certificate the following week

options.text: They said, “They are issuing the certificate the next week.”
They said, “We will issue the certificate next week.”
They said, “Could we issue the certificate the following week?”
They said, “They issued the certificate the following week.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Whenever we convert indirect speech to direct speech, it's important to remember the following points:
 
 
• The conjunction **"That" **should be changed into inverted commas(," ")
 
• Make changes in the **reported speech clause** according to the type of sentence.
 
• Change time and place references like "**that day**" into "**today**", "**the day before**" into "**yesterday**", "**the following week**" into "**next week**", etc.
 
• For example: 
 
 
• He said that he lived in Delhi. (Indirect)
 
• *He said, "I live in Delhi. (direct)*
 
• She said that she would call me the following day. (indirect)
 
• *She said, " I will call you tomorrow. (direct)*
 
 
 
 

Based on the above points & examples, the correct sentence should be "*They said, "We will issue the certificate next week"*.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The poor washerwoman washes dirty clothes from morning to evening.

options.text: Dirty clothes have been washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes were washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes are washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes are being washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Present Indefinite Tense because **"routine & habit" **can be expressed in this tense.

 
 
• In **Passive Voice - Present Indefinite Tense**, we always use the helping verb__ **is/am/are** and __main verb__ **3rd form.**
 
• The** Object **comes in the beginning, and the **doer (subject) **comes with the preposition **"by".**
 
 

Based on the above instructions, the accurate sentence would be "Dirty clothes **are washed** by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The basic rule for Present Indefinite Tense - Passive Voice:
 
 
• Object + is/am/are + verb 3rd form + by + doer (subject).
 
• For example:
 
 
• Rocky cooks food in the morning.
 
• *Food is cooked by Rocky in the morning.*
 
• Robin always speaks the truth.
 
• *The truth is always spoken by Robin.*
 
 
 
 

At last, the correct sentence is "*Dirty clothes are washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening"*.

questions.question:

__
 
• The sentence is in "**Past Indefinite Tense",** and it's an "**interrogative sentence"**.
 
• In such sentences, we always use "**did &** **verb 1st form"**.
 
• So, using verb 2nd form *i.e. **kept**, *is **inappropriate **here.

We should use **'Where did you keep', **instead of **'Where did you kept'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The basic rule for Past Indefinite Tense (Interrogative Sentence):-

 
• Wh family + did + subject + verb 1st form + object?
 
 
• Why **did **you **go **there? not (went there)
 
• Where **did **you **meet **him yesterday?
 
• How **did **you **solve** that sum?
 
 

Hence, the correct sentence is *"**Where did you keep** the sack of wheat that I bought from the market"?*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

There was a bell over the door __that jingled whenever__ a customer entered
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, there is a **connection between** a noun '**a bell**' and a clause **'jingled whenever a customer entered'.**

 
 
• **'Relative pronoun - that' **is always used to connect a clause or phrase with people or things.
 
 

The given sentence is accurate, so there is no substitution required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• in **'Option 1 - which jingled wherever',** a wrong conjunction **'wherever'** can be seen that makes no sense with the given sentence,
 
• In **'Option 2 - who jingles whenever', **an incorrect relative pronoun **'who' **can be seen that is** used for people** only, **not for the object** like a bell.
 
• In **'Option 3 - that jingle when'**, we can see the wrong usage of** tense 'jingle'** and **conjunction 'when', **whereas the given sentence is in **the past tense**.

Based on above points, **No substitution** is required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Relative pronouns like **'Who' or 'Which' ** always connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun.
 
• **'Who' **is always used for people. For example, I know the person **who **lives here.
 
• **'Which' **is always used for objects & animals. For example, My mobile, which I bought last week, is lost.

Hence, the correct sentence is 'There was a bell over the door **that jingled whenever** a customer entered.*
